REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) / SOURCES SOUGHT ANNOUNCEMENT 

  DEPARTMENT OF THE NAVY  
 Program Acquisition Executive Mission Systems (PAE MS)  
 Capability Portfolio Executive Combat Systems & Fires (CPE CS&F)   
 Integrated Combat System (ICS), PMW 630  

 SECTION 1: GENERAL INFORMATION 

  Document Type:  Request for Information (RFI) / Sources Sought Notice 

  Solicitation / Reference Number:  N6175027R1201 

  Contracting Activity:  Navy PAE Mission Systems, Washington Navy Yard, DC 

  Program Title:  Surface Ship ICS Engineering and Integration 

  North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code:  541330 – Engineering Services (Military and Aerospace Equipment and Military Weapons) 

  Product Service Code (PSC):  AC13 – R&D: Defense Systems: Weapons / R425 – Support - Professional: Engineering/Technical 

  Response Due Date:  04 December 2026, 15:00 EST 

  Classification Level:  Primary document UNCLASSIFIED. Classified responses or annexes up to SECRET / NOFORN handled by separate coordination (see Section 7). 

 SECTION 2: STATUTORY DISCLAIMER & SPECIAL NOTICE 

 This RFI is issued solely for  information and planning purposes  in accordance with  FAR 15.101(c) . 

 This notice does  not  constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or an announcement of a forthcoming solicitation. Issuance of this notice does not obligate the Government to issue a formal solicitation or award a contract. 

 The Government will  not  pay or reimburse any costs incurred by respondents in preparing, submitting, or demonstrating information in response to this notice. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. 

 Participation in this RFI is voluntary. Failure to respond will not preclude a vendor from participating in any future competitive acquisition, should one be released. 

 Respondents may submit capability statements addressing  any subset or all  of the focus areas detailed herein. 

 SECTION 3: BACKGROUND & PROGRAM CONTEXT 

  3.1 Background & Context  

 Modern surface warfare requires rapid, modular capability delivery across the Navy's surface fleet. The Navy’s ICS program is making this vision a reality through use of virtualization, Kubernetes orchestration, and development of a common suite of mission applications enabling a "build once and deploy across the fleet" methodology for delivery of capability to frigates, destroyers, amphibious ships, aircraft carriers, future manned and unmanned vessels, and future foreign military sales vessels. 

 The ICS program is conducting market research to identify industry partners capable of executing comprehensive systems engineering and software integration for U.S. Navy surface combat systems.  This scope is currently being executed under the N00024-23-C-5117 contract awarded to Lockheed Martin Rotary & Mission Systems in September 2023. 

  3.2 Technical Scope & Baselines  

 The technical scope spans current and next-generation baseline configurations running incremental deliveries of the Integrated Combat System (ICS) software stack (infrastructure services and tactical platform services) and common mission applications.  Applicable ship deliveries include the following: 

 
	 ICS-Enabled AEGIS Combat System Baselines 9.C3+ and Baseline 10.1+ running on Mk6 Mod0/1 hardware with IaaS ORDALT or on Mk6 ModX hardware 
	 ICS-Enabled Ship Self-Defense System (SSDS) platforms 
	 FF(X) 3 and follow 
	 DDG 1000 class in line with delivery of the Zumwalt Enterprise Upgrade Solution (ZEUS) 
	 Future USN and FMS platforms 
 

 SECTION 4: TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS & CAPABILITY AREAS SOUGHT 

 The Navy seeks detailed technical capabilities, corporate competencies, and innovative methodologies across eleven (11) functional areas. Vendors may respond to  any or all  of the following scope areas: 

  Focus Area 1: Programmatic Engineering, Configuration Management & Governance  

 
	  Configuration Management (CM):  Formulating, baselining, and executing Configuration Management Plans (CMP), software build/release planning, Configuration Control Boards (CCBs), and tracking and adjudicating Software Change Requests (SWCRs). 
	  Programmatic & Systems Planning:  Developing, maintaining, and synchronizing project-level Roadmaps, Integrated Master Schedules (IMS), and capability delivery cadences. 
 

  Focus Area 2: Systems Engineering & Requirements Architecture  

 
	  Technical Baseline Artifacts:  Developing, updating, and managing formal engineering artifacts: 
	 Systems Engineering Plans (SEP). 
	 Software Development Plans (SDP) utilizing modern Agile/DevSecOps frameworks. 
	 System / Subsystem Definition Documents (SSDD). 
	 System / Subsystem Specifications (SSS). 
	 Software Product Specifications (SPS). 
	 Interface Requirements Specifications (IRS). 
	 Requirements Traceability Verification Matrices (RTVM) maintaining end-to-end bidirectional requirement-to-test traceability. 
	 System Safety Plans (SSP) conforming to MIL-STD-882E and naval weapon safety requirements. 
	  Requirements Allocation:  Decomposing ICS, AEGIS, SSDS, and future combat system Top Level Requirements (TLR) into modular capability building blocks and subsystem specifications across surface ship classes (DDG 51, CG 47, FF(X), DDG 1000, L-Class, CVN, unmanned surface vessels, FMS variants, future platforms). 
	  Technical Leadership:  Serving as lead technical authorities in Integrated Product Teams (IPTs), Working Groups (WGs), formal milestone reviews (SRR, PDR, CDR), and leading Technical Interchange Meetings (TIMs) to define and allocate interface requirements. 
	  Force-Level Mission Thread Analysis:  Evaluating complex, distributed kill-chain mission threads, establishing functional allocations, and resolving tactical latency challenges. 
	  ICS Re-Architecture & Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE):  Author
